title: Pair Duplication with a Space Bound
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the pair encoding of $(x,x)$: each bit of $x$ doubled, followed by the separator $01$, followed by $x$. For every Boolean word $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the computation through step $t$ uses at most $c$ work-tape cells.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of a finite Turing machine over Booleans
Existence of a natural-number constant c
Computes the pair encoding of (x,x) within c(|x|+1) steps on every input
For every input and every t, space through step t is at most c
